steps.content:
September 2, N.F. 115
Eastside District 3, Augustus Mansion (formerly Peace Mansion)
Victory Celebration Banquet for the Ash Campaign
Since last year's attack on the Viers Mansion, the historic Peace Mansion has emerged as the district's most prestigious venue for elite gatherings. Tonight, it is a monument to extravagance.

Gold and silver horse statues stand beside blooming flowers. Bottles of fine wines gleam under the light as rare blue feathers adorn legendary swords and armor, all competing for attention. The air is thick with the cloying scent of perfume, a fragrance so potent it stings the nose.

In every corner, wealth is immolated in a desperate race to express adoration for the General's victory. The guests have collectively decided this is the style she prefers—a questionable assumption, at best.

They are here to celebrate her triumph, but the true cause for revelry is the mansion's renaming. Several distinguished elites have even swallowed their pride, trading formal wear for blue military attire. It is as if, from this day forward, "Peace" has been superseded by a more glorious name: Augustus.
Yet, beneath the celebratory veneer, the air crackles with a faint, restless anxiety.

steps.speaker: Guest
steps.content: Are we really safe with her here? She's not like the others... And it wasn't long ago that we...

steps.speaker: Guest
steps.content: Shh! She's a woman of grand ambition, not some petty tyrant. And anyone who can't see which way the wind is blowing is a fool. It's just like the Independence War. Stake your claim now or get left behind.

steps.speaker: Guest
steps.content: Unlike that idiot Max King, he's really... Oh! Look, she's here!
The star of the evening makes her entrance. General Augustus descends the grand staircase, her opulent gown a seamless part of the bejeweled tapestry of political and business elites below.
In a deliberate irony, the guest of honor herself has forgone her signature, flamboyant military regalia, rendering the banquet's meticulous martial theme a case of profoundly misguided flattery.

All eyes follow her as she glides through the crowd, not to greet a dignitary, but to stop before a decorative suit of armor in the corner. You watch, helpless, as she "invites" you out from your hiding spot behind it and decisively links her arm with yours.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: You're early. Excited, aren't you?
She smiles with intimate familiarity, as if she has entirely forgotten that you two nearly came to blows in the interrogation room just yesterday.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: It's <color=#fb9259>Catherine</color>.

She hasn't just forgotten; she's orchestrating a scene. Deliberately, she steps closer, her hands coming up to straighten your posture with a proprietor's air. Under the weight of the crowd's gaze, she begins to adjust you.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: We went over this last night. Still can't get your tie straight?
steps.female_content: We went over this last night. Your hair's come loose again.

steps.content: With a knowing smile, she focuses on your collar, standing so near that her presence is a physical force. A mere downward glance captures the intimate details: the silk of her hair, the sweep of her lashes, the elegant line of her nose, and her vivid red lips...
steps.female_content: With a knowing smile, she tucks the stray hairs at your temples behind your ears. Her wrist brushes your cheek, carrying with it that familiar, subtle fragrance—a scent that irresistibly draws your gaze back to her face.

steps.content: She has always been radiant, but at this proximity, the fearsome general reveals an unexpected tenderness. Her fingertips brush against your throat, a touch so light it forces you to tilt your head back, a futile attempt to escape her overwhelming brilliance.
steps.female_content: She has always been radiant, but at this close distance, surrounded by her fragrance, the fearsome battlefield commander unexpectedly reveals an unfamiliar tenderness. It doesn't take her long to arrange your hair, but then her fingertips trail lightly down the curve of your ear. A jolt of sensation sparks through you, forcing you to turn your head away from her intense scrutiny—

steps.content: —only to be met by the stares of the crowd, their faces now a mask of envy and admiration.

steps.speaker: Guest A
steps.content: What a stunning pair, the heroes of our city! You simply must grace the cover of our magazine. We'll arrange our finest photography team for you.

steps.speaker: Guest C
steps.content: Beyond that, the General's heroic deeds will surely be recorded in the history books, celebrated for generations, just like Keylan... Oh, I can already picture the illustrations!

steps.speaker: Guest B
steps.content: "Augustus Breaching BR-005"—The Frank family has already commissioned DisCity's most renowned artist to capture the moment. The masterpiece will be delivered to your residence the instant it's complete.

The flattery finds its mark. The valorous general leans against you, shaking with laughter as she pulls you into the spotlight. The socialites, usually so cunning, now spew the most absurd praises, which she accepts with regal grace.

This is the treatment Catherine Augustus Andohar now commands in DisCity. Bathed in this cloying, suffocating adoration, only she could accept it as her natural birthright. You, however, dragged along like a royal consort, can only squirm in misery.

options: We had a "good time" last night?

choices.text: We had a "good time" last night?

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: Heh. Just giving the fools a little show. Don't you think their reactions are amusing?
The fools in the audience savor every moment of her staged scandal, their faces plastered with sycophantic glee.
She answers with a smile, her grip a silent command not to leave.
Just then, a distinctly prominent voice cuts through the chorus of sycophantic praise.

steps.speaker: Wilton
steps.content: General, your presence truly honors this gathering. And of course, your esteemed companion as well.

The man offers a respectful bow in your direction. You recognize him from a memorial reception. <color=#fb9259>Wilton Stewart</color>, a prominent conservative councilor who was outmaneuvered by Max King twice—first in an election, then in the recent war. Now, he is swiftly repositioning himself for a new gambit, a man not to be underestimated.
The crowd instinctively parts, granting the host the coveted space before the General, a privilege he accepts with natural ease. Noting your empty hands, he smoothly continues.

steps.speaker: Wilton
steps.content: I have a treasured vintage, imported from the Campbell Estate. Might it be to your taste?

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: Hmm... a bit too dry for me. I prefer something sweeter.

steps.speaker: Wilton
steps.content: Of course, right away. And you, Chief of the MBCC? Any preferences?

steps.speaker: Wilton
steps.content: I must say, I never dreamed both heroes of our city-state would grace us with their presence tonight. It's an immense honor. Please accept my personal gratitude.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: Hehe, you're as accommodating as ever. But our little ${PlayerName} doesn't drink this kind of stuff. Let's talk about something else.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: If I recall, you invited me here to discuss something important. Something about my garrison?
Wilton freezes mid-gesture, shooting a furtive, almost guilty glance in your direction.

steps.speaker: Wilton
steps.content: Well... I had hoped to be better prepared, to discuss this in the privacy of your residence. And since Chief ${PlayerName} is honoring us for the first time, surely there are more interesting diversions. My collection room, or the gallery?
As he elaborates on his generous invitation, his eyes steal another look in your direction. Catherine, having missed nothing, allows a knowing smile to form.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: Should I call you a coward, or just blind? Can't you see? ${PlayerName} came here with me. That makes this person no outsider... and I don't appreciate that kind of treatment.
Wilton freezes for only a moment before a sudden understanding dawns, his face brightening with unmistakable delight.

steps.speaker: Wilton
steps.content: Oh! Oh, of course! How foolish of me. You two are steadfast allies, comrades who have faced death together. That makes you both my most honored friends! Please, right this way—
He eagerly leads you both toward another man.

steps.speaker: Sernie
steps.content: General Augustus. And... Chief ${PlayerName}.
Bowing to you, he shares a swift glance with Wilton, and his own defenses finally come down.

steps.speaker: Sernie
steps.content: I am Sernie. As for my background... heh, let's just say it's not the most important detail tonight. What is important is the word on the street, that General Augustus's troops are still lodged in a hotel.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: The finest hotel in Eastside.

steps.speaker: Sernie
steps.content: Naturally. The wealth of the Andohar family is truly remarkable.

steps.speaker: Sernie
steps.content: However... for a distinguished hero of the city-state to lack a proper garrison within our own walls... it would make DisCity a laughingstock if word got out.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: Well then, enlighten me. Where do you believe the DisCorps's new garrison should be established?
They immediately take the subtle depth in her smile for encouragement. Sernie clears his throat and seizes the opportunity.

steps.speaker: Sernie
steps.content: The FAC was fundamentally built around the DisCorps, integrating numerous other departments. And there's no question that you and your Shattered Blade are the rightful heirs to that legacy. You never should have been separate entities to begin with.

steps.speaker: Sernie
steps.content: We are at war now. The FAC can no longer confine itself to internal affairs. If your forces were to fight side by side, with close coordination, it would tremendously enhance the security of our entire city-state...

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: That's not for you to decide, is it?
As Sernie smiles, you observe a ripple effect; one by one, the faces behind him mirror the expression.

steps.speaker: Sernie
steps.content: It's not my decision alone, but the will of the people. The calling of our era. These are extraordinary times; DisCity needs a wartime leader to guide us all and usher in a new age.

steps.speaker: Sernie
steps.content: The Commander has grown old. Set in his ways. I believe there is no one in all of DisCity more suited to the role than you.

steps.speaker: Sernie
steps.content: The business sector, the city council, and even... certain voices from Paradeisos all want you to step forward. Or, at the very least, have your forces take a definitive position on the garrison. Should you show interest, many would eagerly clear the path for you...

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: Well then... I thank you both for your... consideration.

Her smile deepens as she raises her glass in a toast of agreement with the two men, wholly ignoring the tension in your arm. It is the signal they have been waiting for. A palpable wave of relief washes over the crowd, and the room slowly fills with the hum of laughter and animated conversation.

steps.speaker: Guest B
steps.content: You know, looking back, this war hasn't been all bad. The whole West District situation has made the economy stagnant for years, but the General's forces have turned it all around overnight. The Outlands took quite the beating this time. And the war reparations... care to guess the figure?

steps.speaker: Guest C
steps.content: Heh, the reparations are nothing. The real prize is BR-005. They deployed all those Apostles of Ashes... and after suppressing them, there are supposedly no mines? Impossible. Mark my words, a new great Hypercube rush is about to begin.

steps.speaker: Guest C
steps.content: If that's true, with General Augustus at the helm, our shipping lanes will be secure, trade will flow, and our military power will be completely revitalized! It's time to cast off the shackles of history and forge a new world order...

At this moment, victory has finally descended upon DisCity. The air is thick with intoxicating flattery, a tribute the flushed and excited crowd offers up like courtiers to a newly crowned queen. The hall vibrates with a shared fantasy: the spoils of war and a glorious future for all.

The fear is gone. Now, from the shadows of high society, countless hands reach for her—like putrid, grasping flesh drawn to a gleaming blade. They rejoice that its edge no longer presses their throats, and celebrate as it is now poised to conquer the world for them.

steps.speaker: Wilton
steps.content: There is... one more small matter...

steps.speaker: Wilton
steps.content: It's just that recently, the Speaker and that 9th Agency have been talking about investigating asset transfers, Outland dealings... How should I put this... don't you think they're going a bit too far?

steps.speaker: Wilton
steps.content: Not all financial transactions are suspicious! Some are just delayed settlements. If this continues, innocent people will be caught in the crossfire. The war is over. We should be unified, not creating division. All I'm saying is...

As the man stammers his excuses, a wave of nausea washes over you. You look away, only to find the entire room is doing the same—a sea of carefully neutral masks, all ears intently trained on the General, waiting. A roomful of scum, all cut from the same rotten cloth.
In response, Augustus offers only the ghost of a smile, an answer as ambiguous as silence.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: You'll have to ask my dear Chief about that. The Euphoria investigation was his initiative, after all. Better stay on his good side, hmm?
steps.female_content: You'll have to ask my dear Chief about that. The Euphoria investigation was her initiative, after all. Better stay on her good side, hmm?

steps.content: Wilton's gleaming eyes immediately snap to you, fixing on you with a look of desperate, calculating eagerness.

steps.speaker: Wilton
steps.content: Thank you so very much—
His face lights up with delight, and he launches into a torrent of words. The flood of filth that was meant for Augustus instantly gushes toward you.
Just as you reach your limit and move to brush his hand away, Augustus leans close to your ear once more, an intimate, possessive gesture, like someone jealously reclaiming what is hers.
He leans in, his face greasy and shining, provoking a violent wave of goosebumps across your skin. The sensation is more violating than a Corruptor's attack.
Just as you reflexively move to brush his hand away, Augustus leans close to your ear once more, an intimate, possessive gesture, like someone jealously reclaiming what is hers.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: Well, I've enjoyed myself long enough. I still have somewhere to be with my dear ${PlayerName} for the second round.

steps.speaker: Sernie
steps.content: Huh? Leaving so soon? But we still have so much to discuss about the garrison...

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: I said, it's long enough.

A slight chill falls over the moment. Sernie, catching the signal at once, swiftly pivots the conversation. And so, Augustus smiles at him again. A generous smile, the kind given to a well-trained dog for performing a trick.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: It's such a lovely evening. I want to show him my private collection. Sorry, but this time, I want it to be just the two of us.
steps.female_content: It's such a lovely evening. I want to show her my private collection. Sorry, but this time, I want it to be just the two of us.

steps.content: At these words, the guests fall silent, then—spurred by the quick-witted—erupt into applause.
They shower you with cheesy praises, from "feast for the eyes" to "kindred spirits," lauding the DisCorps-MBCC alliance and the union of its two heroes.

steps.speaker: Guest C
steps.content: Have a wonderful night!
Then, to rowdy cheers, Augustus downs her wine and flings the empty glass into the throng. In the chaotic scramble for the souvenir, she links her arm with yours and makes her escape.
[Exit and get into the car]
[Exit and get into the car 2]

You are in yet another of the General's luxury cars, cruising through the heart of the bustling city. But this time, your stomach churns with a violent dread, every nerve on edge. In the driver's seat, Augustus is the picture of relaxation, as if it were all just the norm.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: Phew... remind me, who was that person again?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: A key figure in the Council's conservative faction. Wilton Stewart. Distant relative of the former Speaker. And the other one, Sernie, seems to have connections that could help you... stir the pot with the FAC.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: They're trying to provoke you into seizing FAC territory for a garrison station and using the opportunity to usurp power and expand your influence.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: Oh, right. See? Bringing you along was a brilliant move. Very clever. Make a note of them.
Keeping track of such people feels like a stain on the mind, yet you commit their faces and names to memory regardless.
With a general as unpredictable as her, you can never know when she might finally be swayed by their honeyed words and decide their schemes have merit.

options: I had no idea you enjoyed these kinds of events.

choices.text: I had no idea you enjoyed these kinds of events.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Is the <color=#fb9259>second round</color> going to have the same stench? Don't you find it all a bit disgusting?

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: Not at all. I come from a military arms dynasty. I've been used to it since I was a child.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: Wherever there's money and power, people will always claw their way in. So much naked ambition in one place... of course it feels dirty to you.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: But as you climb higher, your world will only get more crowded. So much praise and flattery, so many schemes and desires... Especially here in DisCity. You'll be put on a pedestal and constantly subjected to the worst of human nature.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: Better get used to it now. Build up your immunity. I'd hate to see the day our noble Chief gives in to temptation and is wracked with guilt over it.

options: I could always choose to keep my distance.

choices.text: I could always choose to keep my distance.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: Haha. How do you expect to change the world while avoiding the battlefield? Besides... you can't escape anyway.

Augustus stretches her arm into the slipstream, her hand riding the howling DisCity wind. Behind her extravagant sunglasses, her gaze is fixed on the road ahead, yet seems to look through it into some vast nothingness. The glittering city lights slide over her face, streaking past so that light and shadow perform an ambiguous dance across her features.
In the lull between the rushing wind and the engine's hum, her soft words are almost lost:

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: You've had a long night. Let me take you home.
[Scene Change: MBCC Office]

September 3, N.F. 115, 10:00 AM
MBCC Chief's Office
Before you can fully piece together the clues from the previous day, an uninvited guest arrives at the MBCC office.

The visitor is <color=#fb9259>Kane Diesel</color>, a media professional known for covering politics. You have no personal recollection of him, but his name comes with a referral from a friend of Max King. After a moment's deliberation, you grant him entry.
The moment he sits down, he gets straight to the point.

steps.speaker: Kane
steps.content: There's a lot of chatter in the city-state about Augustus taking over the FAC and restructuring the military. Chief, what's your take? Is it even feasible? Credible?
Is he referring to the Rancor troops formally relocating back within DisCity? Your instincts go on high alert, but you keep your expression perfectly neutral.

options: ...That's well above my pay grade. No comment.

choices.text: ...That's well above my pay grade. No comment.

steps.content: Kane raises an eyebrow.

steps.speaker: Kane
steps.content: Really? Your department works with both sides more than almost anyone. Any shake-up would land directly on your doorstep. You can't tell me you're not concerned.

steps.speaker: Kane
steps.content: Or is it... an uncomfortable topic? Given your... close relationship with General Augustus?
You shoot a glare at him.

steps.speaker: Kane
steps.content: Sorry, I mean no offense. It's just, when people see you two at the banquet together last night, they'll talk. It's only natural.

steps.speaker: Kane
steps.content: And that obvious favor she shows you... That's a significant opportunity, isn't it?
What are you implying?

steps.speaker: Kane
steps.content: Look, setting aside the historical baggage and just focusing on power, the city-state is desperate for military strength right now. Combat departments are on the rise. They've been held back by the FAC's bureaucracy. But this? This could be a chance to reshuffle the entire deck...

steps.speaker: Kane
steps.content: Right now, General Augustus is in a league of her own. She's the talent the city-state needs, and the one most likely to claim the largest piece of the post-war pie. Align with the right faction, and you catch the prevailing wind.

steps.speaker: Kane
steps.content: Her iron will, her decisiveness—her exceptional abilities in every regard. She reminds me of Marshal Dravyn in his prime. Setting aside the historical baggage, she's destined to be the brightest star of our future.

"Setting aside the historical baggage"—he's said it twice now. The hypocrisy is glaring; it's clear the "baggage" is the very reason he's here. He's backing the dictator's heir, betting she will seize power just as her predecessor did.
The realization turns your stomach, but he prattles on, utterly oblivious to your disgust.

steps.speaker: Kane
steps.content: The only question is her next move. Chief, given your rapport with her... have you heard any whispers about her plans, or...
As he talks, he closes the distance between you. Memories of last night's banquet assault your senses, and you feel the last of your patience shatter.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Back off. The mind games you play with her won't work on me.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You want to use the post-war chaos and her momentum to dismantle the FAC, don't you? Start at the garrison, send a signal, and slowly encroach? You see her ambition as a lever you can pull, luring her into your web.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Let me be clear. I may be "fortunate" enough to have her attention, but I will never support her seizing power. I'll stand in her way. That's what a real friend would do!

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You should trust that General Augustus will make the right decision on her own. If she chooses to favor you, my interference won't sway her. Likewise, her ambitions have no influence on me. There is simply no connection between us.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I apologize, but I have a considerable amount of work to attend to. Please see yourself out.
You fire back with a directness that leaves Kane speechless. But his stunned expression is short-lived, quickly replaced by a look of unmistakable relief.

steps.speaker: Kane
steps.content: That's a big relief... You really are as upright and trustworthy as he described.
He dips his head briefly, and when he looks up, the Editor-in-Chief is a different man. His expression sobers, his gaze sharpens, and he fixes you with an unnervingly direct stare.

steps.speaker: Kane
steps.content: I apologize, Chief. That was a test. The current political climate is dangerous. Had you shown even the slightest agreement with my earlier suggestions, I would have had to end the conversation here.

steps.speaker: Kane
steps.content: But now, I'm beyond glad to see we share the same objective: we must firmly oppose this regression. Augustus has to be stopped.
While explaining, he produces a second terminal and swiftly initiates an encrypted link. The screen flickers to life, revealing a face you find familiar.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: We met at the peace ball before the war... You're the Council's recording clerk who opposed Augustus even during wartime. <color=#fb9259>Barry Orwell</color>, is it?
Barry nods, his expression deeply troubled.

steps.speaker: Barry Orwell
steps.content: The DisCorps's occupation of FAC headquarters will be a blatant declaration of ambition. Whether they intend to subjugate the FAC or merge with it to reconstitute the military, the outcome would be earth-shattering. Such a move absolutely requires proper procedural deliberation.

steps.speaker: Barry Orwell
steps.content: But her current behavior, the circles she frequents... it's deeply concerning. If she continues to surround herself with these opportunistic sycophants, the General will inevitably follow her predecessor down the same path. Power is a trap.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...Are you disappointed in her current actions?

steps.speaker: Barry Orwell
steps.content: ...Disappointment would be easier to bear. I must admit, the city-state needs her strength now. And I also... still hope that what she said back then was sincere.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: So what if I try to seize power later? Then stand up to me like you are now. Show some backbone against intimidation. Unite and drive me back. It's that simple. That backbone is exactly why I chose you.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Have you already forgotten the courage you just showed?
A shared, reflective silence falls between you, solidifying into an unspoken alliance. It's you who finally breaks it, after a long moment.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...I feel the same way.
You recount your observations from the banquet and voice your concerns.
Augustus is, by nature, forthright and passionate; you refuse to believe she would stoop to such underhanded schemes for power. If she had wanted that, she could have seized it long ago.

Yet, you cannot be sure how many sycophants now cling to her, drawn by her influence. These opportunists, with their honeyed words, could slowly corrupt her judgment, blind her to reality, and ultimately exploit her until they drag her down into the abyss.

steps.speaker: Barry Orwell
steps.content: I'll continue my media campaign, speaking frankly and exposing those parasites clinging to her. But as she herself pointed out, that alone isn't enough. I must also find a way to stop her.

steps.speaker: Barry Orwell
steps.content: So please, you must speak to General Augustus yourself. You have considerable influence over her. She admires your integrity. Go to her with those qualities. Warn her. Prevent her from falling into the same traps.

steps.speaker: Barry Orwell
steps.content: Thank you... I hope she'll lead the DisCorps down the right path this time. That is the only way to heal the wounds that divide us.
The communication ends. You sink back into your chair, absorbed in your thoughts. Throughout it all, your visitor, Kane, has been watching you with an unwavering focus.
He is the one who finally breaks the silence.

steps.speaker: Kane
steps.content: I fully understand your position now, Chief. I have several old friends in the Council. When the time comes, an alliance with them will make our work much smoother.

steps.speaker: Kane
steps.content: ...I didn't expect you to be so resolute. Without you, I fear the General would have fallen under their influence much sooner.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Me?

steps.speaker: Kane
steps.content: Oh, think nothing of it. I'm counting on you to persuade the General. If you need any assistance from me, just say the word.

Kane takes his leave. As he goes, he casts repeated glances back your way, his expression that of a man who has staked all his hopes on a single card. And after today's conversation, you have to admit, your own perspective has begun to shift...
[Scene Change]

September 4, N.F. 115, 10:00 PM
Eastside Suburbs, Nameless Bar

Your destination is not a luxurious mansion or a high-society venue, but a secluded old house at the end of a quiet, suburban Eastside street. The area is nearly deserted; the few pedestrians are ghosts in the night, and the lone parked sedan is deliberately inconspicuous.

As you ascend the steps, the door swings inward before you can even knock. A woman of modest yet unmistakable elegance greets you. She seems to have been expecting your arrival, and she immediately begins to apologize.

steps.speaker: Owner
steps.content: I'm sorry, we're closed for the evening. If you could please...

steps.speaker: Voice from Inside
steps.content: Since he found his way here on his own, he deserves a reward. Let him in.
steps.female_content: Since she found her way here on her own, she deserves a reward. Let her in.

steps.content: You recognize that voice. The owner offers an apologetic smile and gestures for you to enter.

Stepping inside is like crossing into another world. Candlelight flickers, its glow refracting through the liquor bottles to cast intimate, colorful patterns across half the room. Vintage music drifts from a mobile terminal, the only concession to the modern era in a space otherwise devoid of electricity—a small sanctuary untouched by DisCity's relentless progress.
The booths, which should be filled with patrons, stand completely empty. The only occupant is a familiar figure seated at the bar.

She wears a floor-length red dress, her long hair flowing over her shoulders. Catherine gently swirls her glass, her expression hidden in the play of shadow and dim candlelight. You approach and take the seat beside her.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I asked Iron Mask where I could catch the <color=#fb9259>second round</color>. He gave me this address. Told me to come alone, keep a low profile. I think I managed.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Not a bad spot at all.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: Right? It's peaceful. With our reputations, finding a little privacy is a battle in itself.

options: You could've just come to the Bureau.

choices.text: You could've just come to the Bureau.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Last I checked, you said the interrogation room was very private.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: Please. Your place has ears behind every wall. It's an iron cage. Who'd want to stay for fun?

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: If I ever did set up shop there, I'd have to gut the place first. Give it some actual taste.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: With that metal horse you sent me?

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: Hah. Alright, enough circling. You never seek me out without trouble on your heels. Go on, I'm listening.
As if on cue, the owner serves you the house special. You take a small, deliberate sip, using the moment to collect your thoughts.

options: Do you remember Sernie? Or Wilton?

choices.text: Do you remember Sernie? Or Wilton?

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: Who?
A smile touches your lips. Whether it's the drink or the vibe, a wave of relaxation washes over you, and you wave a dismissive hand.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Never mind. They're nobody.

options: What about Barry Orwell? Ring a bell?

choices.text: What about Barry Orwell? Ring a bell?

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: Oh, that daring recording clerk.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: In your current wave of public admiration, his book, The Dark Side of DisCity: Rule of Shadow, was nearly out of print before the war. Now, it's shot to the top of the bestseller list.
Surprise flashes across the general's face.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: So... congratulations to him?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: "Congratulations"? This wasn't your doing? It's exactly your style, anonymously buying up copies and flooding the districts. You nearly scared the poor clerk to death. He thought it was a threat.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: Oh come on, he's got a spine! Shouldn't a critic with that much talent find a real audience? I'm sick of all this praise. I needed something with more bite. Let all the bootlickers get a taste of it, too.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: Want me to send you a copy? Aren't you quite interested in that sort of history?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Already bought it. Let's talk about something else.

options: Discuss official FAC business with her
Actually enjoy talking about anything with her

choices.text: Discuss official FAC business with her
Actually enjoy talking about anything with her

steps.content: Without a moment's hesitation, you sit beside Augustus and launch into the speech you've been mentally rehearsing, your tone solemn and convinced.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I know all about those people and their real intentions... And I know that you're actually... But when it comes down to it, the point is...

Even you begin to find your lengthy monologue a bit tedious. To your surprise, Augustus—notorious for stirring up trouble—doesn't interrupt. She simply listens, quiet and attentive, before suddenly bursting into unfiltered laughter.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: Look at you, so serious. You and <color=#fb9259>Adrian</color> are cut from the same cloth.
That name... Is it the Commander-in-Chief?
The conversation flows effortlessly, wandering from her Nirvana Port to your Minos, from WhiteSands to Syndicate. Time slips away unnoticed, the well of topics seemingly bottomless.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: Heh, quite the talker... just like <color=#fb9259>Victor</color>.
Victor? The name rings a bell from Barry's bestselling exposé.
In her hand, the ornate glass sways gently, its ice cubes clinking a soft accompaniment to the faint smile on her lips.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: You know <color=#fb9259>Adrian</color>, don't you? FAC Commander-in-Chief, technically your former boss. Let me tell you a secret...

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: He's had that old man demeanor since he was twenty.
She laughs, eager to tell you more.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: Meticulous and rigid in everything, except when he argued with Dravyn. That's when his voice would hit a new peak. And when those two went at it, only Victor could ever pull them apart.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: Victor... the legendary messenger who picked up skills from all over. He could speak anyone's language—talk to saints like a saint, devils like a devil. Even the most troublesome soldiers were putty in his hands.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: With that masterful talent for heart-soothing, if he'd had a shred of malice, the Independence Army would've crumbled from the inside.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: Dravyn should count himself lucky to have had those two. With that stubborn, radical streak of his, he'd have been a real danger without someone to rein him in.
The General's fingers tap a light, rhythmic pattern against her glass. A certain softness in her gaze suggests the drinks are beginning to take effect.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: Me?

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: I was in charge of stirring up trouble. Gave them something new to argue about, kept things from getting dull.

steps.speaker: Owner
steps.content: Heh...
A soft laugh escapes the owner. As she collects your nearly empty glasses, she gently asks her most distinguished regular.

steps.speaker: Owner
steps.content: What would you like this time?

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: That's up to him.
Catherine brushes the triviality aside. Instead, she turns to you, tilting her head as her gaze meets yours, and poses her question.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: Enjoying the stories? Well, now it's your turn. Tell me about yourself, and the people you keep around. I'm all ears.
The answer rises to your lips instinctively, an almost reflexive openness, but you bite it back just in time.
There is something else, something more important, you need to say.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: That day in the interrogation room, you asked why I'd take a mission to investigate you if I wasn't interested in politics.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I didn't have an answer for you then. But I think I do now.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You have a... magnetism. A power to make people feel seen, to inspire loyalty. And that's precisely why I can't ignore the shadows that might lurk beneath.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: That "sweet scent of power" you mentioned? To me, it stinks. And it's dangerous. You're too sharp not to see through their depravity. So why entertain them? Are you buying their flattery, or do you have your own game?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: The more I respect you, the more it unsettles me. And yet... I remember fighting at your side. A part of me wants to silence these doubts, to prove the general I admire is real.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Even now, tonight... I still hope the Augustus I've come to know isn't a facade. I want to trust you.

options: Instead of becoming your enemy someday.

choices.text: Instead of becoming your enemy someday.

steps.content: She listens in absolute silence, her gaze locked with yours. The eye contact holds, stretching the moment, before she finally breaks it with a soft, downward smile.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: That question... is one you'll have to answer for yourself.
She listens quietly, her eyes holding yours. Seeing your unwavering gaze, a fond warmth lights her expression. Then, she reaches over and playfully ruffles your hair.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: Since you put it that way... fine, I'll indulge you.
And so, that is how DisCity's most illustrious General Augustus spends a peaceful night in an obscure, nameless bar, doing nothing at all.
[Scene Change]
Three days later, you see her again—this time, on television.
[Sound of TV being turned on]

steps.speaker: Reporter
steps.content: General! General Augustus! A moment, please! The rumors say the Shattered Blade is officially relocating to DisCity. Congratulations! Could you share more—

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: Oh? And who told you that?

steps.speaker: Reporter
steps.content: Eh? Well... it's common knowledge by now! It's a well-deserved honor for our war heroes, and something the public has been hoping for.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: "Honor"? If that's what we're calling it now, DisCity's standards have certainly fallen. You can keep your rewards. My troops and I will find our own fun.

steps.speaker: Reporter
steps.content: Huh... Your mindset seems to have changed, General. Has someone been... influencing you? Could it be the Chief of the MBCC...?

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: Heh. Think what you want. I do have a few friends, and with them around, it's hard for me to stray from the right path even if I wanted to.
[Scene Transition: Back to Chief's Perspective]
As the interview concludes to the sound of audience applause, you switch off the screen. You turn off the screen just as a call from an old friend comes through.

steps.speaker: 9th
steps.content: A positive outcome, it seems. If this encourages General Augustus to settle into her role, it could bring stability back to the situation.

steps.speaker: 9th
steps.content: After all, should another major conflict arise, she remains our most indispensable military asset.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Something about it feels off. She was just performing, playing with the public. All that serious investigation on our end, and she treats it like a game.

steps.speaker: 9th
steps.content: That sounded almost like a complaint between friends. Does she enjoy teasing you in particular, Chief?

steps.speaker: 9th
steps.content: But you can rest assured, Chief. While General Augustus may be headstrong, she is never disingenuous. Her respect for you is entirely authentic. She would never truly deceive you, at least according to my superior.

steps.speaker: 9th
steps.content: Thank you for helping to guide her back, Chief ${PlayerName}.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I had nothing to do with it. That was definitely all an act on her part. Next time we meet, I'll be having a serious conversation with her...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: But before that, we have other guests to attend to.
Outside the window, a car swerves through the rain, accelerating violently to cut you off. Then, vehicles from behind and the side slam into position, sealing you in a moving trap.
Through the downpour and the glare of headlights, the dark muzzles of several guns stare back at you.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Chief!

Your eyes dart, taking in the situation: you're trapped on a high-speed elevated highway. Three hostile vehicles have you pinned from the front and rear. The only possible exit is the guardrail, and beyond it, a sheer drop of dozens of meters.
In that case, there's only one option...

options: Ram them out of the way!

steps.content: CRASH!! The impact shunts the enemy car sideways, grinding it to a halt. Your reinforced Bureau vehicle shudders but holds, while the attacker's hood crumples, engine spewing black smoke.
Their doors fly open. For a final stand or a frantic escape, it's irrelevant. Shadows detach from the darkness, quickly pinning them down.

The Shattered Blade soldiers move with lethal grace, neutralizing the attackers before they can even react. One assassin receives special attention: Iron Mask seizes him by the throat and slams him onto the ruined hood.

steps.speaker: Attacker
steps.content: Easy... I-I was just a hired gun! I didn't know the target, or that they were connected to DisCorps!

steps.speaker: Attacker
steps.content: Please, spare me! I'll tell you everything!

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...They couldn't even send professionals? How insulting.
Nightingale's expression, however, is etched with deep concern—not for the present danger, but for what this attack implies about your future safety.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: ...Will attempts like this become a regular occurrence?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Let them come. None of them is a real threat. I don't need the Shattered Blade to protect me either. Your efforts are wasted on me. Frankly, for all I know, you might be the ones drawing this trouble to my door.
You shoot a glance at Iron Mask, ready with your usual taunt. But the barb dies on your lips as he remains silent this time.
His body is rigid, a coiled spring, and the surrounding soldiers have fallen into an unnerving silence—their combat stance. Something is wrong.

You track his gaze. A luxury car accelerates from the far end of the road, screeching to a halt nearby. Augustus emerges and strides directly toward you. Her eyes sweep over you, confirming you're unharmed, then shift to her adjutant. Iron Mask is already at attention, his report prepared.

steps.speaker: Iron Mask
steps.content: He wasn't the only target. Of the 11 councilors who voted against the second mobilization, three are now detained on fabricated charges. Also...
steps.female_content: She wasn't the only target. Of the 11 councilors who voted against the second mobilization, three are now detained on fabricated charges. Also...

steps.speaker: Iron Mask
steps.content: <color=#fb9259>Barry</color>, the recording clerk, was attacked at home. He just came out of critical condition.

steps.speaker: Barry Orwell
steps.content: Thank you... I hope she'll lead the DisCorps down the right path this time. That is the only way to heal the wounds that divide us.

Iron Mask passes a comm device to Augustus. A familiar voice crackles over the line. It's the Shattered Blade's doctor, reporting Barry's status. They arrived later than planned, but not too late to save him.

steps.speaker: Military Doctor
steps.content: The assassin was reckless. They were clearly going for the kill.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Do we know who's behind this?

steps.speaker: Iron Mask
steps.content: Those who wanted you to replace the FAC. They're panicking since you backed out. They're likely trying to find out who influenced you.

steps.speaker: Iron Mask
steps.content: Wilton, Sernie, and all guests from the banquet two weeks ago are under Siglinde's surveillance. Also, regarding the attempt on the MBCC Chief...

steps.speaker: Iron Mask
steps.content: Of the recent suspicious visitors to the Bureau, the magazine editor <color=#fb9259>Kane</color> is the prime suspect.
—Kane? The same man who presented himself as part of Augustus's opposition, with his cautious probing, his righteous counsel, and his talk of placing his hopes in you?

steps.speaker: Kane
steps.content: Oh, think nothing of it. I'm counting on you to persuade the General. If you need any assistance from me, just say the word.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...What's this about? He came to MBCC with Barry and urged me to speak out against you.

steps.speaker: Iron Mask
steps.content: He was testing your allegiance. Kane is an actor. His public criticism of Augustus is a cover to infiltrate opposition circles, including Barry's. His media outlet is secretly funded by Wilton's group.

steps.speaker: Iron Mask
steps.content: You're unfamiliar with how these vipers in silk suits hunt. We are not.
The iron lump has finally remembered to talk back, but you're in no mood to engage.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: So they're systematically identifying opponents and eliminating them? Using these... underhanded methods? And these people are loyal to you? They want you in power? Why?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Wait... If that's the case, did you infiltrate their circles to uncover their real agenda?
You look to Augustus for an answer, but she gives no sign of having heard. The headlights behind her backlight her uniformed silhouette, throwing an immense, long shadow across the ground.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Excellent... All these people... Not a single one can be missed.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...What do you want to do?

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Hmm, did I worry you? My apologies.
Her face remains unreadable, shrouded in shadow.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: MBCC personnel, guard your Chief well. The shooter was an amateur, but who knows what else is waiting in the dark.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Well then, I have matters to attend to and won't be seeing you for a while. Take care of yourself, Chief.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: When I return, you'd better be in one piece. Understood?
She offers no answer. A contingent of soldiers insists on escorting you back to the Bureau, while the rest depart with her. For a long time afterward, you receive no news from the Shattered Blade.
The first day passes. Then the second. The third. The fourth...
On the fifth day, you finally find your answer splashed across the news.

<i>Early morning, September 12, N.F. 115: Wilton Stewart was abducted from his estate. No valuables were taken, but all transaction records from his associated accounts were illegally accessed.
Early morning, September 12, N.F. 115: Sernie Parker vanished. Paradeisos issued a notice confirming his office had been ransacked, every document seized.
Early morning, September 12, N.F. 115: Kane Diesel's magazine office was violently broken into. Kane himself disappeared, while detailed records of his political funding sources were systematically leaked online.
Early morning, September 12, N.F. 115: Disturbances were reported around the Andohar family estate. Witnesses observed numerous armed forces entering and leaving the property.

<i>All evidence from these incidents points directly to the Shattered Blade that has remained in the city.

2:00 PM, September 12, N.F. 115: 
Catherine Augustus Andohar stormed the city council with her forces and seized control of the entire building.
<i>It is in this moment that the people of DisCity feel the chilling truth: the shadows of the past have returned, shrouding their city once more.
